newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end down in consolidation phase.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end down in consolidation phase.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower as blue chip and small cap stocks entered a consolidation phase, analysts said.
"We are happy with the consolidation phase. We would be concerned if it had continued to go up," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas.
The benchmark Composite Index fell 2.11 points to 1,218.07, while the small-cap Second Board Index ended just 0.28 points up to 575.06.
Newly-listed BCB Bhd closed at 4.36 ringgit, after debuting at 4.90 ringgit, on an offer price of 1.80 ringgit.

Banking and finance stocks that were requoted on Monday were mixed on Tuesday. Kwong Yik was down 15 cents to 9.00 ringgit, DCB Holdings was down 35 to 8.40, Rashid Hussain was down 10 to 16.60, while Maybank was up 1.50 ringgit to 26.75.
"The banking stocks have done approximately what we expected them to do on being requoted," said Stephen Weller, director of strategy at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
Volume was thinner than recent trading sessions, with 179 million shares traded, valued at 1,386 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 411 to 172, with 141 stocks remaining unchanged.
